{"notes": "Visit 6 (ended 9:00). Picture: the dark chain is unbroken from START over the top, round the nose, along the belly, over the peak and down to a tail tip at about (27.3, 14.7). The belly stray at (13.7, 15.3) is gone and the belly now reads dark and connected, but I didn't see who fixed it. Two pale strays still sit beside the tail at about (24.5-25.2, 12.6-13.2). The tail tip is crowded and could stall. Nobody mentioned the strays this visit.

Tom: Said at 8:30 he nudged the tight tail domino. At 8:45 he said there was still a gap at the tip and he was closing it, 'then hands off, promise'. He has now promised a hands-off twice and is still working at the tip with a push minutes away. The tail did extend, so the work is real, but I can't tell which pieces were his. Still to ask: what did he place, and what are the pale pieces beside the tail? Credit is provisional.

Priya: Good time and process management (two-minute call, step-back before the push). But 'nearly everything falls from the start' is a vague estimate. She called the tail a single tight domino and missed the pale strays. Her earlier 1:45 top-line contradiction is still open. Collaboration is good; execution is unverified.

Leo: Said 'looks good from here' and reinforced hands-off and step-back. He didn't visibly check the belly or tail strays himself. Earlier leadership (the overlap warning) is still verified. This visit he was more of a spectator than a checker.

Maya: Absent and silent again. Her belly-join check is unconfirmed, so there's no basis to rate her beyond what little I saw earlier.

Next: watch the push and see where it stalls, if it does. Ask each person what they placed. Don't rate anyone on the final result alone."}
